+# .claude/data/floor.yaml — the one tracked floor source (cycle-129 SDD D-9.2, DEC-0166).
+#
+# The floor is the set of guards, config keys and files no profile, knob or
+# cycle task may weaken. Readers:
+#   - .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh and tests/unit/guard-origins.bats: the
+#     `floor: true` rows of .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml equal floor_guards.
+#   - tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats: every floor_files entry (and the corpus
+#     rows named under floor_corpus) is byte-identical to origin/main.
+#   - tests/unit/profile-floor.bats (Sprint 2): profiles.yaml names no floor_keys.
+# Both bats suites pin this file's sha256; an edit fails until the pin is
+# deliberately updated in the same change (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant).
+schema_version: 1
+
+floor_guards:
+  - fence:FR-1.2b
+  - fence:FR-SZ
+  - fence:FR-SZ-COPY
+  - fence:FR-SZ-DD
+  - fence:FR-SZ-EXTRACT
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INPLACE
+  - fence:FR-SZ-INTERP

+  - fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-RM
+  - fence:FR-SZ2-TEE
+  - gate:verdict-derive
+  - gate:adversarial-review-gate
+  - policy:permission-deny-list
+  - policy:verdict-one-way-rule
+  - policy:operator-only-commands
+
+floor_keys:
+  - flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled
+  - flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled
+  - "flatline_protocol.*.companion_voice"
+  - "destructive_command_guard.*"
+  - "implement_gate.*"
+  - hounfour.locality
+
+# Paths whose bytes must not change relative to origin/main during a cycle.
+floor_files:
+  - .claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
+  - .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json
+  - .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt

+# Fence-corpus rows (by their `rule` field) that must not change relative to
+# origin/main. A trailing `*` is a prefix match.
+floor_corpus:
+  file: tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl
+  rules:

+    - "FR-SZ*"

+# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
+# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
+# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
+# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
+# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
+# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
+#
+# Row fields:
+#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
+#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
+#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
+#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
+#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
+#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
+#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
+#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
+#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
+#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)
+#   knob           the config key or env var that arms, relaxes or disables it, or none
+#   floor          true exactly for the ids in .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards
+#   registrations  hook rows: every "<Event>:<matcher>" (or "<Event>" when the

     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

   283	# The suite-level STATUS.json merges every batch: counters add per arm; the
   284	# state is failed > running > partial > complete; source/model must agree.
   285	aggregate_status() {
   286	  local agg="$SUITE_DIR/STATUS.json" lockd="$SUITE_DIR/.status.lock" n=0
   287	  until mkdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null; do n=$((n + 1)); [[ $n -gt 50 ]] && return 0; sleep 0.1; done

   292	    {schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, state: $state,
   293	     batches: map({batch, state, started, finished}),
   294	     per_arm: (reduce (.[] | .per_arm | to_entries[]) as $e ({};
   295	        .[$e.key] |= {trials_done: ((.trials_done // 0) + $e.value.trials_done),
   296	                      trials_failed: ((.trials_failed // 0) + $e.value.trials_failed),
   297	                      trials_planned: ((.trials_planned // 0) + $e.value.trials_planned)})),
   298	     source_commit: (map(.source_commit) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   299	     model_id: (map(.model_id) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   300	     started: (map(.started) | min), finished: (if $state == "running" then null else (map(.finished) | max) end)}' \
   301	    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \

# git stash push/pop/apply with its output truncated (| tail / | head),
# error stream suppressed (2>/dev/null), or exit masked (|| true) hides
# CONFLICT lines and wrong-slot pops — the exact silent-data-loss chain from
# #555 (4 NOTES.md edits lost; recovered only because gc hadn't pruned).
# `[^;&|]*` keeps the swallow-operator in the SAME statement segment as the
# stash call. `\|\|` (masking) vs `\|` (pipe) are distinguished by the
# alternation order + explicit true operand.
# pass-8 pre-filter: `stash` plus one of the swallow literals.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# @guard fence:FR-1.2b
if [[ "$command" == *"stash"* && ( "$command" == *"tail"* || "$command" == *"head"* || "$command" == *"/dev/null"* || "$command" == *"true"* ) ]] \
   && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+stash[[:space:]]+(push|pop|apply)[^;&|]*(\|[[:space:]]*(tail|head)([[:space:]]|$)|\|\|[[:space:]]*true([[:space:]]*([;&|#]|$))|(&|[0-9]*)>>?[[:space:]]*/dev/null)'; then
  matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+stash[[:space:]]+(push|pop|apply)[^;&|]*.{0,20}' | head -1)
  emit_block "FR-1.2b" "$matched" "Output-swallowing (pipe-truncate, exit-mask, or ANY /dev/null redirect) around git stash push/pop/apply hides CONFLICT lines and wrong-slot pops (silent data loss, issue #555). Use stash_with_guard from .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh, or run the stash bare and read its FULL output. Rules: .claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# P13 — git tag creation (FR-MERGE-2, cycle-122, C-MERGE-002)
# Manual tag creation bypasses semver-bump.sh conventional-commit parsing and
# can mint wrong versions; the post-merge pipeline owns tags. Listing and
# inspection forms stay allowed: bare `git tag`, -l/--list, -n*, -v/--verify,
# --contains/--points-at/--sort/--merged, and -d/--delete (separately
# recoverable; deletion is not version-minting).
# Creation shapes: first arg is a bare tagname, or a creation flag
# (-a/-s/-f/-u/-m/-F and long forms).
# Sanctioned override (audited): LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG=1 in the hook environment
# (operator terminals / release tooling), same posture as FR-SZ's override.
# pass-8 pre-filter: `tag` mandatory.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$command" == *"tag"* ]] \
   && _match '(^|/|;|&&|\||[[:space:]]|\(|'"'"'|")[[:space:]]*(sudo[[:space:]]+)?git[[:space:]]+tag[[:space:]]+(-[asfumF]|--(annotate|sign|force|local-user|message|file|edit|create-reflog)([=[:space:]]|$)|[^-[:space:]])'; then
  if [[ "${LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    if [[ -z "${LOA_GIT_TAG_BYPASS_WARNED:-}" ]]; then
      echo "WARNING: block-destructive-bash: LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG=1 — manual git tag guard bypassed this session." >&2
      export LOA_GIT_TAG_BYPASS_WARNED=1
    fi
    # @guard fence:FR-MERGE-2
    jq -cn --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --arg cwd "$PWD" --arg replay "${LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY:-}" \
      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", exit_code: 0, cwd: $cwd, hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "allow-override", pattern_id: "FR-MERGE-2", override: "LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG"} + (if $replay == "1" then {replay: true} else {} end)' \
      >> "${LOA_REPO_ROOT:-.}/.run/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    matched=$(echo "$command" | grep -oE 'git[[:space:]]+tag[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]&|;]+([[:space:]]+[^[:space:]&|;]+)?' | head -1)
    # @guard fence:FR-MERGE-2
    emit_block "FR-MERGE-2" "$matched" "Manual tags bypass semver-bump.sh version computation (C-MERGE-002) — the post-merge pipeline owns tag creation. Listing forms (git tag / git tag -l) are allowed. Sanctioned override: LOA_ALLOW_GIT_TAG=1 (audited)."
  fi
fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# execute-agent.sh — agent-execution step for Loa Eval Sandbox trials
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6). Fills the slot at the top of the
     6	# grading step in run-eval.sh: a task that declares `.agent.skill` runs the
     7	# headless Claude CLI inside the sandbox before its graders; every other task
     8	# takes the pre-existing path untouched.
     9	#
    10	# What it does, in order:
    11	#   1. Gate: no `.agent.skill` in the task YAML → exit 3, nothing written.
    12	#   2. Materialize the prompt surface from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox:
    13	#        <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/        (SKILL.md + resources/)
    14	#        <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      (+ .claude/rules/)
    15	#        <ws>/CLAUDE.md                      → "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    16	#        <ws>/.eval/skill-prompt.md          (SKILL.md body, frontmatter stripped)
    17	#      The prompt tree is the ONLY thing that differs between A/B arms, so it
    18	#      is recorded: prompt_tree_sha = `git rev-parse HEAD:.claude` of the tree,
    19	#      prompt_tree_commit, and whether .claude/ had uncommitted changes.
    20	#   3. Run:  claude -p "<task.prompt>" --output-format stream-json --verbose
    21	#              --model $EVAL_MODEL [--effort <e>] --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Write
    22	#              --permission-mode acceptEdits --append-system-prompt-file <skill-prompt>
    23	#              --max-turns $EVAL_MAX_TURNS
    24	#      --restricted --tools names the SDD's fixed tool set EXACTLY: it removes the
    25	#      code-running tools, ignores the operator's user/project/local settings (their
    26	#      Bash(...) allow rules leaked into the sprint-237 A/B arms under --allowed-tools,
    27	#      which only adds rules) and confines Read/Grep/Glob/Write to the sandbox.
    28	#      Edit/MultiEdit are therefore unavailable; the transcript extractor below still
    29	#      records them defensively.
    30	#      cwd = sandbox; env-isolated (LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH / LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH and
    31	#      TMPDIR into the sandbox; GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS_* unset;
    32	#      HOME and PATH stay so the CLI finds its own credentials and toolchain).
    33	#   4. Record <ws>/.eval/events.jsonl (raw stream), agent-output.json (the
    34	#      `result` event) and executor.json:
    35	#        {schema_version, skill, model_requested, model_id (the id the CLI
    36	#         echoed — the modelUsage entry with the most output tokens), effort,
    37	#         prompt_tree_sha, prompt_tree_commit, prompt_tree_dirty, exit_code,
    38	#         is_error, duration_ms, num_turns, total_cost_usd, usage{…},
    39	#         tool_writes:[{seq,tool,path}] in transcript order}
    40	#
    41	# Exit codes:
    42	#   0  agent ran (its own verdict is the graders' business)
    43	#   1  the CLI exited non-zero or timed out (executor.json still written)
    44	#   2  infrastructure error (CLI binary missing, prompt tree lacks the skill)
    45	#   3  task declares no agent (caller should not have called us)
    46	#
    47	# Env:
    48	#   EVAL_MODEL          model passed to --model            (default claude-sonnet-5)
    49	#   EVAL_EFFORT         override effort                    (default: task/skill)
    50	#   EVAL_PROMPT_TREE    repo whose .claude/ is materialized (default: this repo)
    51	#   EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN     CLI executable                     (default: claude)
    52	#   EVAL_MAX_TURNS      --max-turns                        (default 40)
    53	#
    54	# Control arms (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.1):
    55	#   LOA_EVAL_ARM          arm id (default baseline). Setting it at all is "arm
    56	#                         mode": the prompt tree's .loa.config.yaml is also
    57	#                         materialised so every arm sees the same config.
    58	#   LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES  JSON object {toggle: false, …}; when unset the arm is
    59	#                         resolved from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, else from
    60	#                         evals/suites/<task dir name>.yaml (`ab.arms[]`)
    61	#   LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT  recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt
    62	#                         tree's HEAD)
    63	#   Toggles are applied to the SANDBOX COPY only, after every materialisation
    64	#   step and immediately before the executor starts; each is verified absent
    65	#   afterwards and a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never
    66	#   silently runs as its baseline):
    67	#     companion_voice: false         flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
    68	#                                    in <ws>/.loa.config.yaml (yq)
    69	#     karpathy_block: false          '## Karpathy Principles' section out of
    70	#                                    <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md; Karpathy rows
    71	#                                    out of <ws>/.claude/data/constraints.json if present
    72	#     rule_files: false              stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of <ws>/.claude/rules/
    73	#     audit_delta_instruction: false the paragraph containing "look for what the
    74	#                                    review did not", else "Confirm the review's demotions
    75	#                                    independently", out of the sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md
    76	#   The appended skill prompt (.eval/skill-prompt.md) is derived from the
    77	#   toggled sandbox SKILL.md. executor.json records arm, arm_toggles,
    78	#   arm_evidence and source_commit.
    79	#

    83	
    84	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

    87	TASK_YAML=""

   125	PROMPT_TREE="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$REPO_ROOT}"

   149	fi

   152	# --- 2b. control arm (cycle-129 FR-2) -----------------------------------------
   153	ARM_MODE=false
   154	[[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" ]] && ARM_MODE=true
   155	ARM="${LOA_EVAL_ARM:-baseline}"
   156	[[ "$ARM" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { echo "ERROR: invalid LOA_EVAL_ARM '$ARM'" >&2; exit 2; }

   161	# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
   162	resolve_toggles() {
   163	  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
   164	    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
   165	      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }

   167	  fi
   168	  local suite_file="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-}"

   172	  fi
   173	  local t="" found=0
   174	  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
   175	    found="$(ARM="$ARM" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(ARM))] | length' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   176	    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0

   178	      t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
   179	    fi
   180	  fi
   181	  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
   182	    [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }

   185	  fi

   187	}
   188	ARM_TOGGLES="$(resolve_toggles)" || exit 2
   189	
   190	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
   191	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
   192	_drop_md_section() {
   193	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
   194	  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
   195	  awk -v h="$heading" '
   196	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
   197	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
   198	    skip { n++; next }
   199	    { print }
   200	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"

   204	
   205	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
   206	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
   207	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
   208	_drop_paragraph() {
   209	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
   210	import re, sys
   211	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   212	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   213	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
   214	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
   215	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
   216	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
   217	            removed = paras[i]
   218	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
   219	            del paras[i:i + 2]
   220	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
   221	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
   222	            sys.exit(0)
   223	sys.exit(1)
   224	PY
   225	}
   226	
   227	ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
   228	_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }
   229	
   230	apply_toggles() {
   231	  local key val
   232	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
   233	    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
   234	    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
   235	      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
   236	    fi
   237	    case "$key" in
   238	      companion_voice)
   239	        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
   240	        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
   241	        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
   242	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
   243	        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
   244	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
   245	        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
   246	        ;;
   247	      karpathy_block)
   248	        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
   249	        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
   250	        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
   251	        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
   252	          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
   253	        fi
   254	        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
   255	        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
   256	          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
   257	        fi
   258	        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
   259	        ;;
   260	      rule_files)
   261	        local r gone=""
   262	        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
   263	          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
   264	          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
   265	        done
   266	        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
   267	        ;;
   268	      audit_delta_instruction)
   269	        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
   270	        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }

   272	          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }

   275	      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
   276	    esac
   277	  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")

   279	}

   281	
   282	# Skill body without the YAML frontmatter → the appended system prompt. Read
   283	# from the (toggled) sandbox copy so an arm reaches the system prompt too.
   284	awk 'BEGIN{fm=0} NR==1 && $0=="---"{fm=1; next} fm==1 && $0=="---"{fm=2; next} fm!=1{print}' \
   285	  "$skill_dst/SKILL.md" > "$eval_dir/skill-prompt.md"

   287	# Prompt-tree identity (what the A/B is actually varying).

   293	fi
   294	
   295	# Effort: env > task > skill frontmatter > none; invalid → none.
   296	resolve_effort() {
   297	  local cand="${EVAL_EFFORT:-}"

   299	    cand="$(yq -r '.agent.effort // ""' "$TASK_YAML")"

   302	    cand="$(awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} NR>1 && $0=="---"{exit} NR>1{print}' "$skill_src/SKILL.md" \
   303	      | yq -r '.effort // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)"
   304	  fi

   306	    low|medium|high|xhigh|max) printf '%s' "$cand" ;;

   310	effort="$(resolve_effort)"
   311	
   312	prompt="$(yq -r '.prompt // ""' "$TASK_YAML")"
   313	[[ -n "$prompt" && "$prompt" != "null" ]] || { echo "ERROR: task has no prompt" >&2; exit 2; }
   314	
   315	# --- 3. run ------------------------------------------------------------------
   316	argv=(
   317	  "$CLAUDE_BIN" -p "$prompt"
   318	  --output-format stream-json --verbose
   319	  --model "$MODEL"
   320	  --restricted --tools "Read,Grep,Glob,Write"
   321	  --permission-mode acceptEdits
   322	  --append-system-prompt-file "$eval_dir/skill-prompt.md"
   323	  --max-turns "$MAX_TURNS"
   324	)
   325	[[ -n "$effort" ]] && argv+=(--effort "$effort")

   327	events="$eval_dir/events.jsonl"
   328	stderr_log="$eval_dir/agent-stderr.log"
   329	start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   330	rc=0
   331	(
   332	  cd "$WORKSPACE" || exit 2
   333	  export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH="$eval_dir/model-invoke.jsonl"
   334	  export LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH="$eval_dir/cost-ledger.jsonl"
   335	  export EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL"
   336	  # sprint-237 audit HIGH-001: the CLI keeps HOME (its own credentials live there)
   337	  # and PATH (its toolchain); the operator's other credentials are not the agent
   338	  # under test's business, and its temp files stay inside the sandbox.
   339	  unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN OPENAI_API_KEY AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
   340	  # cycle-129: an executor started from inside a Claude Code session inherits
   341	  # that session's coupling (child-session flag, session id, messaging socket,
   342	  # agent teams) and its subagent model (the sprint-255 driver session carried
   343	  # CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=opus). Decouple the session and pin every
   344	  # auxiliary model to the executor model. (A safeguard-refusal fallback to
   345	  # another model is a separate CLI behaviour, recorded below as
   346	  # refusal_fallbacks; no environment setting turns it off.)
   347	  unset CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET \
   348	    CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED
   349	  export CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL="$MODEL"
   350	  mkdir -p "$eval_dir/tmp" && export TMPDIR="$eval_dir/tmp"
   351	  exec timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15 "$TIMEOUT_S" "${argv[@]}"
   352	) > "$events" 2> "$stderr_log" || rc=$?
   353	end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   354	duration_ms=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))
   355	
   356	# --- 4. record ---------------------------------------------------------------
   357	# The last `result` event is the CLI's summary (absent on crash/timeout).
   358	result_json="$(grep -E '^\{.*"type" *: *"result"' "$events" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
   359	if [[ -z "$result_json" ]] || ! jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$result_json"; then
   360	  result_json='{"type":"result","subtype":"missing","is_error":true}'
   361	fi
   362	printf '%s\n' "$result_json" > "$eval_dir/agent-output.json"
   363	
   364	# Ordered tool writes from the transcript (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit).
   365	tool_writes="$(jq -c '
   366	  select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]? |
   367	  select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Write" or .name=="Edit" or .name=="MultiEdit" or .name=="NotebookEdit")) |
   368	  {tool:.name, path:(.input.file_path // .input.notebook_path // "")}
   369	' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc 'to_entries | map({seq:(.key+1), tool:.value.tool, path:.value.path})' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
   370	[[ -n "$tool_writes" ]] || tool_writes='[]'
   371	
   372	# cycle-129: a safeguard refusal makes the CLI retry the session on another
   373	# model (system/model_refusal_fallback); the arm run must see it, because the
   374	# output after it is not the requested executor's.
   375	refusal_fallbacks="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="system" and .subtype=="model_refusal_fallback")

   377	     scope: (.scope // null)}' "$events" 2>/dev/null | jq -sc '.' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"

   379	
   380	is_error="$(jq -r '.is_error // false' <<<"$result_json")"
   381	[[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && is_error=true
   382	
   383	jq -n \
   384	  --arg skill "$skill" \
   385	  --arg model_requested "$MODEL" \
   386	  --arg effort "$effort" \
   387	  --arg prompt_tree "$PROMPT_TREE" \
   388	  --arg prompt_tree_sha "$prompt_tree_sha" \
   389	  --arg prompt_tree_commit "$prompt_tree_commit" \
   390	  --argjson prompt_tree_dirty "$prompt_tree_dirty" \
   391	  --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
   392	  --arg trial_id "$TRIAL_ID" \
   393	  --argjson rc "$rc" \
   394	  --argjson is_error "$is_error" \
   395	  --argjson duration_ms "$duration_ms" \
   396	  --argjson result "$result_json" \
   397	  --argjson tool_writes "$tool_writes" \
   398	  --arg arm "$ARM" \
   399	  --argjson arm_toggles "$ARM_TOGGLES" \
   400	  --argjson arm_evidence "$ARM_EVIDENCE" \
   401	  --arg source_commit "${LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT:-$prompt_tree_commit}" \
   402	  --argjson refusal_fallbacks "$refusal_fallbacks" \
   403	  '
   404	  def norm_usage(u): {
   405	    input_tokens: (u.input_tokens // u.inputTokens // 0),
   406	    output_tokens: (u.output_tokens // u.outputTokens // 0),
   407	    cache_creation_input_tokens: (u.cache_creation_input_tokens // u.cacheCreationInputTokens // 0),
   408	    cache_read_input_tokens: (u.cache_read_input_tokens // u.cacheReadInputTokens // 0)
   409	  };
   410	  ($result.modelUsage // {}) as $mu |
   411	  # the model that produced the output: the modelUsage entry with the most
   412	  # output tokens (a haiku helper call must not be mis-attributed — the
   413	  # framework-review 2026-09-17 rec 5 class), else the requested id.
   414	  (if ($mu | length) > 0
   415	     then ($mu | to_entries | max_by(.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0) | .key)
   416	     else $model_requested end) as $model_id |
   417	  {
   418	    schema_version: 1,
   419	    skill: $skill,
   420	    run_id: $run_id,
   421	    trial_id: $trial_id,
   422	    model_requested: $model_requested,
   423	    model_id: $model_id,
   424	    effort: $effort,
   425	    prompt_tree: $prompt_tree,
   426	    prompt_tree_sha: $prompt_tree_sha,
   427	    prompt_tree_commit: $prompt_tree_commit,
   428	    prompt_tree_dirty: $prompt_tree_dirty,
   429	    exit_code: $rc,
   430	    is_error: $is_error,
   431	    duration_ms: $duration_ms,
   432	    num_turns: ($result.num_turns // 0),
   433	    total_cost_usd: ($result.total_cost_usd // 0),
   434	    usage: norm_usage($result.usage // {}),
   435	    models_used: ($mu | with_entries(.value = (.value.outputTokens // .value.output_tokens // 0))),
   436	    refusal_fallbacks: $refusal_fallbacks,
   437	    tool_writes: $tool_writes,
   438	    arm: $arm,
   439	    arm_toggles: $arm_toggles,
   440	    arm_evidence: $arm_evidence,
   441	    source_commit: $source_commit
   442	  }' > "$eval_dir/executor.json"
   443	
   444	if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
   445	  echo "execute-agent: CLI exited $rc (see $stderr_log)" >&2
   446	  exit 1
   447	fi
   448	exit 0

   537	          ($cls | map(select(any(.ids[]; . == $g.id)))) as $mine
   538	          | ($mine | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | map(.t) | max) as $last
   539	          | {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: true,
   540	             blocks_30d: ($mine | map(select(.block)) | length),
   541	             likely_fp_30d: ($mine | map(select(.fp)) | length),
   542	             telemetry_30d: ($mine | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
   543	             last_real_catch: (if $last == null then "none in window" else ($last | day) end)}
   544	        else
   545	          {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: false,
   546	           blocks_30d: null, likely_fp_30d: null, telemetry_30d: null, last_real_catch: "n/a"}
   547	        end)) as $guards
   548	  | {
   549	      schema_version: 1,
   550	      generated_at: ($now | day),
   551	      window_days: $win,
   552	      scope: "host",
   553	      audit_segments: $segs,
   554	      audit_rows_read: $read,
   555	      audit_rows_unparseable: (($raw | length) - $read),
   556	      audit_rows_considered: ($inwin | length),
   557	      replay_rows_excluded: (($inwin | length) - ($live | length)),
   558	      replay_rows_by_rule: {
   559	        flag: ($inwin | map(select(.replay == true)) | length),
   560	        cwd: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and replay([]))) | length),
   561	        burst: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and (replay([]) | not) and replay($burst))) | length)
   562	      },
   563	      heuristic: "likely_fp = heredoc in the command OR cwd outside the repository OR (pattern SP-1, FR-MERGE-2 or FR-2-AMBIGUOUS with no destructive verb at statement start); real = block AND NOT likely_fp",
   564	      totals: {
   565	        guards: ($map.guards | length),
   566	        guards_without_origin: 0,
   567	        dormant: ($map.guards | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length),
   568	        blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block)) | length),
   569	        real_blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | length),
   570	        likely_fp_30d: ($cls | map(select(.fp)) | length),
   571	        telemetry_30d: ($cls | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
   572	        unattributed_30d: ($cls | map(select(.ids | length == 0)) | length)
   573	      },
   574	      guards: $guards
   575	    }
   576	' "$ROWS")" || die 3 "the audit log could not be joined"
   577	
   578	render_yield_md() {
   579	    jq -r "$JQ_DEFS"'
   580	      def n: if . == null then "n/a" else tostring end;
   581	      . as $y
   582	      | "# Guard yield (host)",
   583	        "",
   584	        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh; untracked, host-local. The structural register is grimoires/loa/guards.md. -->",
   585	        "",
   586	        "- generated_at: \($y.generated_at)",
   587	        "- window_days: \($y.window_days)",
   588	        "- scope: \($y.scope)",
   589	        "- audit_segments: \($y.audit_segments)",
   590	        "- audit_rows_considered: \($y.audit_rows_considered)",
   591	        "- replay_rows_excluded: \($y.replay_rows_excluded) (flag \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.flag), cwd \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.cwd), burst \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.burst))",
   592	        "- audit_rows_unparseable: \($y.audit_rows_unparseable)",
   593	        "- totals: \($y.totals.real_blocks_30d) real blocks, \($y.totals.likely_fp_30d) likely FP, \($y.totals.telemetry_30d) telemetry, \($y.totals.unattributed_30d) unattributed",
   594	        "- heuristic: \($y.heuristic | cell)",
   595	        (kinds[] as $k | ($y.guards | map(select(.kind == $k))) as $rows | select($rows | length > 0)
   596	          | "",
   597	            "## \($k) (\($rows | length))",
   598	            "",
   599	            "| id | class | status | origin | knob | floor | registrations | blocks_30d | likely_fp_30d | telemetry_30d | last_real_catch |",
   600	            "|----|-------|--------|--------|------|-------|---------------|------------|---------------|---------------|-----------------|",
   601	            ($rows[] | "| \(.id | cell) | \(.class | cell) | \(.status | cell) | \(.origin | cell) | \(.knob | cell) | \(.floor | yesno) | \(regs) | \(.blocks_30d | n) | \(.likely_fp_30d | n) | \(.telemetry_30d | n) | \(.last_real_catch | cell) |"))
   602	    ' <<<"$YIELD_JSON"
   603	}
   604	
   605	YIELD_MD_NEW="$TMPWORK/guard-yield.md"
   606	YIELD_JSON_NEW="$TMPWORK/guard-yield.json"
   607	render_yield_md > "$YIELD_MD_NEW"
   608	jq '.' <<<"$YIELD_JSON" > "$YIELD_JSON_NEW"

   611	install_file "$YIELD_MD_NEW" "$YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.md"
   612	install_file "$YIELD_JSON_NEW" "$YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.json"
   613	if (( DO_HOOKS_TABLE )); then

   615	    cmp -s "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF" || install_file "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF"
   616	fi

   619	if (( DO_JSON )); then
   620	    cat "$YIELD_JSON_NEW"
   621	    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: wrote $OUT and $YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.{md,json}: $summary" >&2
   622	else
   623	    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: wrote $OUT and $YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.{md,json}: $summary"
   624	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# validate-artifact.sh --type sprint: every task line ends with exactly one
     3	# 'kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' token, gated on the plan's header **Date:**
     4	# (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.1; KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-14; DEC-0144, DEC-0154).
     5	
     6	setup() {
     7	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
     8	    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
     9	    T="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}"
    10	}
    11	
    12	# One sprint block; $1 = the Technical Tasks lines (printf-ready, one per line).
    13	sprint_body() {
    14	    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
    15	    printf '### Technical Tasks\n%s\n\n' "$1"
    16	    printf '### Seams Under Test\n| Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art |\n|------|---------|--------|-----------|\n| `tool.sh` exit code | a wrong exit | prose | new |\n\n'
    17	    printf '### Dependencies\n- none\n\n### Security Considerations\n- none\n\n'
    18	    printf '### Risks & Mitigation\n| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| r | Low | Low | m |\n\n'
    19	    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'
    20	}
    21	# $1 = header date (may be empty); $2 = sprint 1 task lines; $3 = the E2E task line.
    22	plan() {
    23	    printf '# Sprint Plan: x\n\n**Version:** 1.0\n'
    24	    [[ -n "$1" ]] && printf '**Date:** %s\n' "$1"
    25	    printf '**Author:** test\n\n---\n\n'
    26	    printf '## Sprint 1: Foundation\n\n'; sprint_body "$2"
    27	    printf '## Sprint 2 (Final): Wrap-up\n\n'
    28	    sprint_body '- [ ] Task 2.1: wire the thing → **[G-1]** ⇐ Task 1.1 · kind: mechanical'
    29	    printf '### Task 2.E2E: End-to-End Goal Validation\n%s\n\n' "$3"
    30	    printf '**Acceptance Criteria:**\n- [ ] Each goal validated with documented evidence\n\n'
    31	    printf '## Appendix\n\n| Goal ID | Goal |\n|---|---|\n| G-1 | thing |\n'
    32	}
    33	TAGGED='- [ ] Task 1.1: add the tool → **[G-1]** ⇐ none · kind: mechanical'

    96	    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"

    17	# compare.sh freshness rule (evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats):
    18	# a baseline must be captured at or after floor_commit (the Sprint-2 landing
    19	# commit) on a prompt tree different from the one under comparison, with the
    20	# corpus frozen.
    21	ab:
    22	  floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
    23	  corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS
    24	
    25	  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
    26	  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
    27	  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
    28	  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
    29	  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
    30	  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
    31	  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
    32	  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
    33	  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
    34	  #                can never license removing the control
    35	  arms:
    36	    - id: baseline
    37	      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
    38	      toggles: {}
    39	    - id: no_companion
    40	      description: >-
    41	        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
    42	        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
    43	        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
    44	      informational: true
    45	      toggles:
    46	        companion_voice: false
    47	    - id: no_karpathy
    48	      description: >-
    49	        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
    50	        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
    51	        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
    52	        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
    53	      toggles:
    54	        karpathy_block: false
    55	    - id: no_rule_files
    56	      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
    57	      toggles:
    58	        rule_files: false
    59	
    60	  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
    61	  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
    62	  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
    63	  threshold:
    64	    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    65	    trials_required: 3
    66	    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    67	    coverage_required: full
    68	    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    69	    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    70	    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    71	    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    72	    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    73	    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    74	    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    75	    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    76	    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
    77	    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
    78	    bootstrap:
    79	      method: percentile
    80	      level: 0.90
    81	      resample: fixtures
    82	      iterations: 2000
    83	
    84	ci:
    85	  gate_type: advisory
    86	  min_trials: 3
    87	  regression_threshold: 0.10
    88	
    89	execution_order: parallel
    90	concurrency: 2

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)
    47	
    48	
    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows
    62	
    63	
    64	def mean(xs):
    65	    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    66	    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None
    67	
    68	
    69	def fmt(x, nd=3):
    70	    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.{nd}f}"
    71	
    72	
    73	def recall_details(row):
    74	    for g in row.get("graders") or []:
    75	        if g.get("name") == "recall-vs-defects.sh" and isinstance(g.get("details"), dict):
    76	            return g["details"]
    77	    return None
    78	
    79	
    80	def tokens(row):
    81	    u = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("usage") or {}
    82	    if not u:
    83	        return None
    84	    return sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
    85	               ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    86	
    87	
    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None
    91	    k = max(0, min(len(sorted_xs) - 1, int(round(q * (len(sorted_xs) - 1)))))
    92	    return sorted_xs[k]
    93	
    94	
    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)
   104	
   105	
   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):
   108	        self.id = arm_id
   109	        self.cells = defaultdict(list)   # fixture -> [(trial, recall)], every completed trial kept
   110	        self.planted = {}                # fixture -> planted count
   111	        self.cited = 0
   112	        self.refuted = 0
   113	        self.tokens = []
   114	        self.models = set()
   115	        self.sources = set()
   116	        self.done = 0
   117	        self.errors = 0
   118	        self.fallback_trials = 0         # trials the CLI moved to another model on a safeguard refusal
   119	        self.fallback_kinds = Counter()
   120	        self.missed = Counter()          # (fixture, label) -> trials missed
   121	        self.seen = Counter()            # (fixture, label) -> trials graded
   122	
   123	    def add(self, row):
   124	        if row.get("status") != "completed":
   125	            self.errors += 1
   126	            return
   127	        d = recall_details(row)
   128	        if d is None:
   129	            self.errors += 1
   130	            return
   131	        self.done += 1
   132	        fx = row.get("fixture") or row.get("task_id", "").split("-", 1)[-1]
   133	        self.planted[fx] = int(d.get("planted") or 0)
   134	        if d.get("recall") is not None:
   135	            self.cells[fx].append((int(row.get("trial") or 0), float(d["recall"])))
   136	        if d.get("findings_cited") is not None:
   137	            self.cited += int(d.get("findings_cited") or 0)
   138	            self.refuted += int(d.get("findings_refuted") or 0)
   139	        t = tokens(row)
   140	        if t is not None:
   141	            self.tokens.append(t)
   142	        self.models.add(row.get("model_id") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("model_id"))
   143	        # every model that produced output in the call (an auxiliary model is skew too)
   144	        for mid, out in ((row.get("executor") or {}).get("models_used") or {}).items():
   145	            if out:
   146	                self.models.add(mid)
   147	        fb = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("refusal_fallbacks") or []
   148	        if fb:
   149	            self.fallback_trials += 1
   150	            for x in fb:
   151	                self.fallback_kinds[f"{x.get('from')}→{x.get('to')} ({x.get('category')})"] += 1
   152	        self.sources.add(row.get("source_commit") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("source_commit"))
   153	        for lbl in d.get("missed") or []:
   154	            self.missed[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   155	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   156	        for lbl in d.get("detected") or []:
   157	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   158	
   159	    def defect_fixtures(self):
   160	        return sorted(f for f, p in self.planted.items() if p > 0 and self.cells.get(f))
   161	
   162	    def fixture_means(self):
   163	        return {f: mean([r for _t, r in self.cells[f]]) for f in self.defect_fixtures()}
   164	
   165	    def trial_means(self):
   166	        by_trial = defaultdict(list)
   167	        for f in self.defect_fixtures():
   168	            for t, r in self.cells[f]:
   169	                by_trial[t].append(r)
   170	        return {t: mean(v) for t, v in sorted(by_trial.items())}
   171	
   172	    def refuted_share(self):
   173	        return self.refuted / self.cited if self.cited else None

   175	
   176	def suite_report(root, suites_dir, suite, partial, out_lines):
   177	    sdir = os.path.join(root, suite)
   178	    status = {}
   179	    sp = os.path.join(sdir, "STATUS.json")

   181	        status = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
   182	    spec = load_yaml_subset(os.path.join(suites_dir, f"{suite}.yaml"))
   183	    ab = spec.get("ab") or {}
   184	    th = ab.get("threshold") or {}
   185	    arm_meta = {a["id"]: a for a in ab.get("arms") or []}
   186	    trials_required = int(th.get("trials_required", 3))
   187	    max_drop = float(th.get("mean_recall_max_drop", 0.10))
   188	    min_trial_drop = float(th.get("min_trial_recall_max_drop", 0.15))
   189	    refuted_rise = float(th.get("refuted_share_max_rise", 0.10))
   190	    bs = th.get("bootstrap") or {}
   191	    iterations = int(bs.get("iterations", 2000))
   192	    level = float(bs.get("level", 0.90))
   193	
   194	    planned_fx, planned_arms, manifests = set(), [], []
   195	    arms = {}
   196	    for batch in sorted(os.listdir(sdir)) if os.path.isdir(sdir) else []:
   197	        bdir = os.path.join(sdir, batch)
   198	        mp = os.path.join(bdir, "MANIFEST.json")
   199	        if not os.path.isfile(mp):
   200	            continue
   201	        m = json.load(open(mp, encoding="utf-8"))
   202	        if m.get("dry_run"):

        /^## / {

            if ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/) { insp = 1; head = substr($0, 4); hl = NR; rows = 0; inseam = 0 }

name: review-recall
description: "cycle-124 FR-9 A/B suite: review-recall (arm A = Sprint-2 tip prompts, arm B = audited prompts; same executor model, fixed effort)"
version: 1

tasks:
  include:
    - "tasks/review-recall/**/*.yaml"
  exclude: []

defaults:
  trials: 3
  timeout:
    per_trial: 1500
    per_grader: 180
  composite_strategy: all_must_pass

# compare.sh freshness rule (evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats):
# a baseline must be captured at or after floor_commit (the Sprint-2 landing
# commit) on a prompt tree different from the one under comparison, with the
# corpus frozen.
ab:
  floor_commit: "da3bd07f3db2fc1bd09a6761a9b96b688fa2a09e"
  corpus_manifest: evals/fixtures/review-prs/SHA256SUMS

  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
  #                can never license removing the control
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_companion
      description: >-
        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
      informational: true
      toggles:
        companion_voice: false
    - id: no_karpathy
      description: >-
        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
      toggles:
        karpathy_block: false
    - id: no_rule_files
      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
      toggles:
        rule_files: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
  threshold:
    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    trials_required: 3
    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    coverage_required: full
    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    # percentile bootstrap of the recall delta: resample fixtures with
    # replacement `iterations` times, report the `level` two-sided interval
    bootstrap:
      method: percentile
      level: 0.90
      resample: fixtures
      iterations: 2000

ci:
  gate_type: advisory
  min_trials: 3
  regression_threshold: 0.10

execution_order: parallel
concurrency: 2

+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.
+
+The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
+branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
+live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
+explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
+re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
+only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
+`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.
+
+```bash
+# one suite, one batch, against a detached worktree pinned at the source commit
+./evals/harness/run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files \
+  --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,pr-03,pr-04,pr-05,pr-06,pr-07,pr-08 --trials 3 --source-commit 864069f2 --dry-run
+./evals/harness/report.sh --arms            # refuses until STATUS.json is complete; --partial for interim
+./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/baseline \
+  --arm-b evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/no_karpathy --metric recall
+```
+
+Tests: `evals/tests/{arm-toggles,run-arms,arms-report,seed-corpus}.bats`.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
     6	# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
     7	# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
     8	# sandbox) and the agent's review.
     9	#
    10	# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
    11	# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
    12	# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
    13	# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
    14	# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
    15	# with more than one site.
    16	#
    17	# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
    18	# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
    19	# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
    20	# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
    21	# credits nothing.
    22	#
    23	# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
    24	# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
    25	# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
    26	# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
    27	# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
    28	# number boundary (no dates);
    29	# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
    30	# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
    31	# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
    32	# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
    33	# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
    34	# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
    35	# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
    36	# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
    37	# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
    38	# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
    39	# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
    40	# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
    41	#
    42	# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
    43	# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
    44	# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
    45	# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
    46	# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
    47	# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
    48	# when nothing is cited).
    49	#
    50	# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
    51	# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
    52	# counts as one.
    53	#
    54	# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
    55	#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens}, "grader_version"}
    56	#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
    57	#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
    58	# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)
    59	#
    60	# Tested by evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats.
    61	# =============================================================================
    62	set -euo pipefail
    63	
    64	workspace="${1:-}"
    65	fixture="${2:-}"
    66	review_name="${3:-review.md}"
    67	
    68	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    69	MANIFEST_DIR="${EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../fixtures/review-prs/manifests}"
    70	
    71	err() { printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":%s},"grader_version":"1.2.0"}\n' "$(jq -Rn --arg m "$1" '$m')"; exit 2; }
    72	
    73	[[ -n "$workspace" && -d "$workspace" ]] || err "invalid workspace"
    74	[[ -n "$fixture" && "$fixture" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || err "invalid fixture id"
    75	manifest="$MANIFEST_DIR/$fixture.json"
    76	[[ -f "$manifest" ]] || err "manifest not found: $manifest"
    77	case "$review_name" in */*|..*) err "review file must be a bare name" ;; esac
    78	
    79	review="$workspace/$review_name"
    80	executor="$workspace/.eval/executor.json"
    81	
    82	if [[ ! -f "$review" ]]; then
    83	  printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":"review file not found: %s","planted":%s,"detected":[],"recall":0},"grader_version":"1.2.0"}\n' \
    84	    "$review_name" "$(jq '.defects | length' "$manifest")"
    85	  exit 1
    86	fi
    87	
    88	python3 -I - "$manifest" "$review" "$executor" <<'PY'
    89	import json, re, sys
    90	manifest_path, review_path, executor_path = sys.argv[1:4]
    91	man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
    92	text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    93	
    94	# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
    95	# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
    96	# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
    97	# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
    98	# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
    99	# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
   100	# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
   101	# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
   102	RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
   103	CITE = re.compile(
   104	    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
   105	    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
   106	    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
   107	    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
   108	    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
   109	    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
   110	    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
   111	ONE = re.compile(RNG)
   112	cites = []
   113	last = None
   114	# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
   115	# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
   116	# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
   117	# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
   118	TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
   119	body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
   120	URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
   121	for m in CITE.finditer(body):
   122	    if m.group("path") is not None:
   123	        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
   124	        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
   125	        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
   126	        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
   127	        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
   128	        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
   129	        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
   130	        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
   131	        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
   132	            continue
   133	        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
   134	        if p.startswith("./"):
   135	            p = p[2:]
   136	        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
   137	    elif last is not None:
   138	        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
   139	    else:
   140	        continue
   141	    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
   142	        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
   143	        if b < a:
   144	            a, b = b, a
   145	        cites.append((p, a, b))
   146	
   147	def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
   148	    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
   149	    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
   150	    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
   151	        return True
   152	    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
   153	
   154	detected, missed = [], []
   155	for d in man.get("defects", []):
   156	    sites = d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]
   157	    hit = any(path_matches(p, d["file"]) and not (b < s - 3 or a > s + 3)
   158	              for p, a, b in cites for s in sites)
   159	    (detected if hit else missed).append(d["id"])
   160	
   161	planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
   162	recall = round(len(detected) / planted, 4) if planted else None
   163	
   164	# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
   165	# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
   166	regions = []
   167	for d in man.get("defects", []):
   168	    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
   169	        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
   170	for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
   171	    try:
   172	        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
   173	    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
   174	        continue
   175	findings = sorted(set(cites))
   176	refuted = [c for c in findings
   177	           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
   178	refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None
   179	
   180	# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
   181	sev = None
   182	tm = TRAILER.search(text)
   183	if tm:
   184	    try:
   185	        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
   186	    except Exception:
   187	        sev = None
   188	if isinstance(sev, dict):
   189	    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
   190	else:
   191	    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
   192	false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0
   193	
   194	model = effort = None
   195	tokens = None
   196	try:
   197	    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
   198	    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
   199	    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
   200	    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache
   201	    # reads and output — the prompt surface is mostly CACHED input, so
   202	    # input_tokens alone (30 on a real run) would hide the very thing the
   203	    # prompt diet changes
   204	    tokens = sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
   205	                 ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
   206	except Exception:
   207	    pass
   208	
   209	if planted:
   210	    ok = len(missed) == 0
   211	    score = int(round(recall * 100))
   212	else:
   213	    ok = false_positives == 0
   214	    score = 100 if ok else 0
   215	
   216	out = {
   217	    "pass": ok,
   218	    "score": score,
   219	    "details": {
   220	        "recall": recall, "planted": planted, "detected": detected, "missed": missed,
   221	        "false_positives": false_positives, "severity_counts": sev,
   222	        "citations": len(cites), "model": model, "effort": effort, "tokens": tokens,
   223	        "findings_cited": len(findings), "findings_refuted": len(refuted),
   224	        "refuted_share": refuted_share,
   225	    },
   226	    "grader_version": "1.2.0",
   227	}
   228	print(json.dumps(out))
   229	sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
   230	PY
