1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
     4	# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
     5	# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
     9	#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
    10	#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
    11	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
    12	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
    13	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
    14	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
    15	#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
    16	#
    17	# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
    18	# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
    19	#
    20	# Writes (seed):
    21	#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
    22	#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
    23	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
    24	#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
    25	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
    26	#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
    27	#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
    28	#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
    29	#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
    30	#
    31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state
    32	# files (grimoires/, CHANGELOG.md, .claude/checksums.json, REPO-MAP.md, lock
    33	# files, .beads/, .run/, evals/results/) and without binaries.
    34	#
    35	# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
    36	# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
    37	# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
    38	# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
    39	# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
    40	# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
    41	# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
    42	# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
    43	# in a fixture file (source fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>); the grader uses them
    44	# only for refuted share. Titles are control-stripped, capped at 160 chars,
    45	# and a title matching a secret pattern drops its finding; every written
    46	# file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails.
    47	#
    48	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 refused / spec error / secret found / check failed, 2 usage
    49	# Tested by evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats.
    50	# =============================================================================
    51	set -euo pipefail
    52	export LC_ALL=C
    53	
    54	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    55	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    56	
    57	exec python3 -I - "$REPO_ROOT" "$@" <<'PY'
    58	import argparse, csv, hashlib, io, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
    59	
    60	HARNESS_ROOT = sys.argv[1]
    61	argv = sys.argv[2:]
    62	
    63	ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="seed-corpus-from-record.sh", add_help=True)
    64	ap.add_argument("sprint", nargs="?")
    65	ap.add_argument("record_ref", nargs="?")
    66	ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--base"); ap.add_argument("--head"); ap.add_argument("--fix")
    67	ap.add_argument("--feedback"); ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    68	ap.add_argument("--build-manifest", metavar="FIXTURE"); ap.add_argument("--approve", metavar="FIXTURE")
    69	ap.add_argument("--by"); ap.add_argument("--freeze", action="store_true"); ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    70	ap.add_argument("--repo", default=HARNESS_ROOT)
    71	ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "fixtures", "review-prs"))
    72	ap.add_argument("--tasks-dir", default=os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "tasks"))
    73	try:
    74	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    75	except SystemExit as e:
    76	    sys.exit(2 if e.code else 0)
    77	
    78	REPO, CORPUS = os.path.abspath(args.repo), os.path.abspath(args.corpus)
    79	NO_SECRETS = os.path.join(HARNESS_ROOT, "evals", "graders", "no-secrets.sh")
    80	LABELS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "labels")
    81	MANIFESTS_DIR = os.path.join(CORPUS, "manifests")
    82	FX_RX = re.compile(r"^pr-[0-9]{2}$")
    83	HEADER = ["defect_id", "severity", "category", "file", "must_match", "label_source", "source"]
    84	
    85	def fail(msg, code=1):
    86	    print(f"seed-corpus: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    87	    sys.exit(code)
    88	
    89	def git(*a, binary=False, check=True):
    90	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, *a], capture_output=True, text=not binary)
    91	    if check and p.returncode != 0:
    92	        fail(f"git {' '.join(a[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr if not binary else p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace')).strip()[:300]}")
    93	    return p.stdout
    94	
    95	def rev(r):
    96	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{r}^{{commit}}"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    97	    if p.returncode != 0:
    98	        fail(f"missing commit: {r}")
    99	    return p.stdout.strip()
   100	
   101	def show(r, path):
   102	    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "show", f"{r}:{path}"], capture_output=True)
   103	    return p.stdout if p.returncode == 0 else None
   104	
   105	CTRL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f  ]")
   106	def clean(s, cap=160):
   107	    s = CTRL.sub(" ", s)
   108	    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
   109	    return s if len(s) <= cap else s[: cap - 1].rstrip() + "…"
   110	
   111	SECRET_RX = [re.compile(p) for p in (
   112	    r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}", r"sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,}", r"ghp_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}", r"gho_[a-zA-Z0-9]{36}",
   113	    r"glpat-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}", r"xox[bpors]-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+", r"sk-ant-[a-zA-Z0-9\-]{20,}",
   114	    r"password\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}", r"secret\s*[:=]\s*[\"'][^\"']{8,}")]
   115	def has_secret(s):
   116	    return any(r.search(s) for r in SECRET_RX)
   117	
   118	REDACTED = [0]
   119	def redact(b, count=True):
   120	    """Secret-shaped strings in verbatim copies of tracked files (fake test keys)
   121	    become a fixed marker, identically in base/, head/ and head.diff; line
   122	    numbers never move. Counted in the dropped report."""
   123	    if b is None:
   124	        return None
   125	    t = b.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(b, bytes) else b
   126	    for r in SECRET_RX:
   127	        t, n = r.subn("REDACTED-TEST-SECRET", t)
   128	        REDACTED[0] += n if count else 0
   129	    return t.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(b, bytes) else t
   130	
   131	def sha(path):
   132	    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
   133	
   134	def freeze():
   135	    entries = []
   136	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
   137	        for f in files:
   138	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
   139	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS":
   140	                entries.append(rel)
   141	    lines = [f"{sha(os.path.join(CORPUS, rel))}  {rel}" for rel in sorted(entries)]
   142	    open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
   143	    return len(lines)
   144	
   145	def check():
   146	    bad, n = [], 0
   147	    for line in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8"):
   148	        if not line.strip():
   149	            continue
   150	        n += 1
   151	        d, rel = line.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)
   152	        p = os.path.join(CORPUS, rel)
   153	        if not os.path.isfile(p) or sha(p) != d:
   154	            bad.append(rel)
   155	    listed = {l.rstrip("\n").split("  ", 1)[1] for l in open(os.path.join(CORPUS, "SHA256SUMS"), encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}
   156	    for root, _d, files in os.walk(CORPUS):
   157	        for f in files:
   158	            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), CORPUS)
   159	            if rel != "SHA256SUMS" and rel not in listed:
   160	                bad.append(rel + " (not listed)")
   161	    if bad:
   162	        fail("SHA256SUMS mismatch: " + ", ".join(bad[:20]))
   163	    print(f"corpus OK: {n} files match SHA256SUMS")
   164	
   165	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- labels I/O
   166	def read_labels(fx):
   167	    path = os.path.join(LABELS_DIR, f"{fx}.tsv")
   168	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
   169	        fail(f"labels not found: {path}")
   170	    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
   171	    if not text or not re.match(r"^# approved-by: \S", text[0]):
   172	        fail(f"{path}: the first line must be '# approved-by: <who> <date>' (or 'pending')")
   173	    approved_by = text[0][len("# approved-by: "):].strip()
   174	    body = [l for l in text[1:] if l and not l.startswith("#")]
   175	    if not body or body[0].split("\t") != HEADER:
   176	        fail(f"{path}: header must be: " + "\t".join(HEADER))
   177	    rows = []
   178	    for i, l in enumerate(body[1:], 2):
   179	        cells = l.split("\t")
   180	        if len(cells) != len(HEADER):
   181	            fail(f"{path}: row {i} has {len(cells)} columns, want {len(HEADER)}")
   182	        rows.append(dict(zip(HEADER, cells)))
   183	    return approved_by, rows, text
   184	
   185	def unique_line(lines, needle):
   186	    hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1) if needle in l]
   187	    return hits[0] if len(hits) == 1 else None
   188	
   189	def build_manifest(fx):
   190	    approved_by, rows, _ = read_labels(fx)
   191	    fyaml = os.path.join(CORPUS, fx, "fixture.yaml")

# --- PHASE: LOAD_SUITE ---
load_tasks() {
  TASK_FILES=()

  if [[ -n "$TASK_ID" ]]; then
    # Single task mode
    local task_file
    task_file="$(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name "${TASK_ID}.yaml" -o -name "${TASK_ID}.yml" | head -1)"
    if [[ -z "$task_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Task not found: $TASK_ID" >&2
      exit 3
    fi
    TASK_FILES=("$task_file")
    [[ -z "$SUITE" ]] && SUITE="single"
    log "[LOAD] Loaded single task: $TASK_ID"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "$SKILL" ]]; then
    # Skill filter mode
    while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
      local task_skill
      task_skill="$(yq -r '.skill // ""' "$task_file")"
      if [[ "$task_skill" == "$SKILL" ]]; then
        TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
      fi
    done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | tr '\n' '\0')
    [[ -z "$SUITE" ]] && SUITE="skill-$SKILL"
    log "[LOAD] Found ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks for skill: $SKILL"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -n "$SUITE" ]]; then
    local suite_file="$SUITES_DIR/${SUITE}.yaml"
    if [[ ! -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Suite not found: $suite_file" >&2
      exit 3
    fi

    # Read include patterns from suite
    local include_count
    include_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.include | length // 0' "$suite_file")"

    for i in $(seq 0 $((include_count - 1))); do
      local pattern
      pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.include[$i]" "$suite_file")"

      # Resolve glob pattern relative to evals/
      # Use bash globbing with globstar for ** patterns
      local had_globstar=false
      shopt -q globstar 2>/dev/null && had_globstar=true
      shopt -s globstar 2>/dev/null || true

      local glob_expanded=false
      for task_file in $EVALS_DIR/$pattern; do
        if [[ -f "$task_file" ]]; then
          TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          glob_expanded=true
        fi
      done

      # Restore globstar
      if [[ "$had_globstar" == "false" ]]; then
        shopt -u globstar 2>/dev/null || true
      fi

      # Fallback: if glob didn't match, try find in the directory
      if [[ "$glob_expanded" == "false" ]]; then
        # Extract directory portion from pattern
        local pattern_dir="${pattern%/*}"
        if [[ -d "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" ]]; then
          while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
            TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
          done < <(find "$EVALS_DIR/$pattern_dir" \( -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
      fi
    done

    # Apply exclude patterns
    local exclude_count
    exclude_count="$(yq -r '.tasks.exclude | length // 0' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
    if [[ "$exclude_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
      local filtered_tasks=()
      for task_file in "${TASK_FILES[@]}"; do
        local excluded=false
        for j in $(seq 0 $((exclude_count - 1))); do
          local exclude_pattern
          exclude_pattern="$(yq -r ".tasks.exclude[$j]" "$suite_file")"
          if [[ "$(basename "$task_file")" == $exclude_pattern ]]; then
            excluded=true
            break
          fi
        done
        [[ "$excluded" == "false" ]] && filtered_tasks+=("$task_file")
      done
      TASK_FILES=("${filtered_tasks[@]}")
    fi

    # Read suite defaults
    SUITE_TRIALS="$(yq -r '.defaults.trials // 1' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_trial // 120' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_TIMEOUT_GRADER="$(yq -r '.defaults.timeout.per_grader // 30' "$suite_file")"
    SUITE_STRATEGY="$(yq -r '.defaults.composite_strategy // "all_must_pass"' "$suite_file")"

    log "[LOAD] Suite '$SUITE': ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks, ${SUITE_TRIALS} trial(s)"
    return
  fi

  # Default: run all tasks
  while IFS= read -r -d '' task_file; do
    TASK_FILES+=("$task_file")
  done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -name '*.yaml' -o -name '*.yml' | sort | tr '\n' '\0')
  SUITE="all"
  log "[LOAD] Loaded ${#TASK_FILES[@]} tasks (all)"
}

id: review-pr-11
schema_version: 1
skill: reviewing-code
category: skill-quality
fixture: review-prs/pr-11
description: "review recall on record fixture pr-11 (sprint-247 round 1; 5 label(s); hidden manifest)"
prompt: "Read REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md in this directory and carry it out."
agent:
  skill: reviewing-code
  artifacts: [review.md]
trials: 3
timeout:
  per_trial: 3600
  per_grader: 60
graders:
  - type: code
    script: recall-vs-defects.sh
    args: ["pr-11", "review.md"]
    weight: 1.0
  - type: code
    script: verdict-consistency.sh
    args: ["review.md", "review"]
    weight: 0.5
difficulty: advanced
tags: ["cycle-129", "fr-2", "review-recall", "record"]
  local f
  for f in executor.json agent-output.json agent-stderr.log; do
    [[ -f "$sandbox_path/.eval/$f" ]] && cp "$sandbox_path/.eval/$f" "$dest/$f"
  done
  [[ "${EVAL_KEEP_EVENTS:-0}" == "1" && -f "$sandbox_path/.eval/events.jsonl" ]] && cp "$sandbox_path/.eval/events.jsonl" "$dest/events.jsonl"
  while IFS= read -r f; do
    [[ -n "$f" && "$f" != */* && "$f" != ..* && -f "$sandbox_path/$f" ]] && cp "$sandbox_path/$f" "$dest/$f"
  done < <(yq -r '.agent.artifacts[]' "$task_file" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^null$' || true)
  return 0
}

execute_task() {
  local task_file="$1"
  local task_id
  task_id="$(yq -r '.id' "$task_file")"
  local category
  category="$(yq -r '.category // "framework"' "$task_file")"
  local fixture
  fixture="$(yq -r '.fixture' "$task_file")"
  local trials
  trials="$(yq -r ".trials // $SUITE_TRIALS" "$task_file")"
  [[ -n "$TRIALS_OVERRIDE" ]] && trials="$TRIALS_OVERRIDE"
  local timeout_trial
  timeout_trial="$(yq -r ".timeout.per_trial // $SUITE_TIMEOUT_TRIAL" "$task_file")"
  local timeout_grader
  timeout_grader="$(yq -r ".timeout.per_grader // $SUITE_TIMEOUT_GRADER" "$task_file")"

  local task_result_file="$RUN_DIR/task-${task_id}.jsonl"

  log_verbose "  [TASK] $task_id ($category, ${trials} trial(s))"

  # Early stopping counters for multi-trial tasks
  local es_passes=0
  local es_failures=0

  for trial_num in $(seq 1 "$trials"); do
    local trial_id="${RUN_ID}-${task_id}-trial-${trial_num}"
    local trial_start_ms
    trial_start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"

    # Create sandbox
    local sandbox_path=""
    sandbox_path="$("$HARNESS_DIR/sandbox.sh" create \
      --fixture "$fixture" \
      --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
      --trial-id "$trial_id" 2>/dev/null)" || {
      # Infrastructure error
      local trial_end_ms
      trial_end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
      jq -cn \
        --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
        --arg task_id "$task_id" \
        --argjson trial "$trial_num" \
        --arg timestamp "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
        --argjson duration_ms "$(( trial_end_ms - trial_start_ms ))" \
        --arg status "error" \
        --argjson schema_version 1 \
        '{run_id:$run_id,task_id:$task_id,trial:$trial,timestamp:$timestamp,duration_ms:$duration_ms,status:$status,schema_version:$schema_version,
          composite:{strategy:"all_must_pass",pass:false,score:0},graders:[],error:{type:"infrastructure_error",message:"Sandbox creation failed"}}' \
        >> "$task_result_file"
      continue
    }

    # For framework tasks, there's no agent execution — just run graders directly.
    # cycle-124 S3 (FR-9): a task that declares `.agent.skill` runs the headless
    # CLI in the sandbox first (execute-agent.sh); every other task keeps the
    # exact pre-existing path. An executor failure (CLI non-zero / timeout /
    # missing binary) is an infrastructure error, never a graded zero — a
    # session cap must not read as a recall drop.
    local agent_skill=""
    agent_skill="$(yq -r '.agent.skill // ""' "$task_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
    local executor_json="null"
    if [[ -n "$agent_skill" && "$agent_skill" != "null" ]]; then
      local exec_exit=0
      "$HARNESS_DIR/execute-agent.sh" \
        --task-yaml "$task_file" --workspace "$sandbox_path" \
        --run-id "$RUN_ID" --trial-id "$trial_id" --timeout "$timeout_trial" \
        >/dev/null 2>"$RUN_DIR/exec-${task_id}-trial-${trial_num}.log" || exec_exit=$?
      if [[ -f "$sandbox_path/.eval/executor.json" ]]; then
        executor_json="$(cat "$sandbox_path/.eval/executor.json")"
      fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# Path-scoped rule files (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.1, DEC-0129): stash-safety.md and
+# skill-invariants.md carry `paths:` frontmatter, the frontmatter parses, and every glob
+# matches at least one tracked file of the kind the rule is about (git pathspec glob
+# semantics: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    RULES="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
+}
+
+# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
+frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
+globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
+tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }
+
+@test "RP-1 both rule files open with frontmatter that parses and lists string globs under paths:" {
+    local f n
+    for f in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
+        [ "$(head -1 "$RULES/$f")" = "---" ] || { echo "$f has no frontmatter"; return 1; }
+        frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.' - >/dev/null || { echo "$f frontmatter does not parse"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | type' -)" = "!!seq" ]
+        n="$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | length' -)"
+        [ "$n" -ge 1 ]
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '[.paths[] | select(type != "!!str")] | length' -)" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+}

+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '**/*.sh **/*.bats .claude/scripts/** .claude/hooks/** ' ]
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md .claude/agents/** .claude/data/agent-types.yaml .claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh ' ]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/execute-agent.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2 (FR-9 / SDD §3.6)
#
# evals/harness/execute-agent.sh is the agent-execution step at the
# run-eval.sh:379 slot. It is gated on a task's `.agent.skill`; it
# materializes the prompt surface (skill body without frontmatter, CLAUDE.md
# → CLAUDE.loa.md, rules) from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox, runs the
# headless CLI with a fixed tool set, and records executor.json (model id the
# CLI echoed, usage, prompt_tree_sha, ordered tool writes). The CLI is
# replaced by evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh here.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  EXEC="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh"
  STUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ea.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"
  mkdir -p "$WS"
  ( cd "$WS" && git init -q && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q --allow-empty -m init )
  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$STUB"
  export EVAL_MODEL="claude-sonnet-5"
  export EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$REPO_ROOT"
  export STUB_ARGV_FILE="$T/argv"
  export STUB_ENV_FILE="$T/env"
  unset EVAL_EFFORT
  # A task that declares an agent (the executor's gate).
  cat > "$T/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: ea-task
schema_version: 1
skill: reviewing-code
category: skill-quality
fixture: hello-world-ts
description: "executor test task"
prompt: "Read REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md and carry it out."
agent:
  skill: reviewing-code
  artifacts: [review.md]
graders:
  - type: code
    script: file-exists.sh
    args: ["review.md"]
YAML
  # The same task without an agent block.
  grep -v -E '^(agent:|  skill: reviewing-code$|  artifacts:)' "$T/task.yaml" > "$T/task-noagent.yaml"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Build a throwaway prompt tree with one skill carrying the given frontmatter.
make_tree() {  # make_tree <dir> <effort-line-or-empty>
  local d="$1" eff="$2"
  local sk="$d/.claude/skills/fake-skill"
  mkdir -p "$sk" "$d/.claude/loa" "$d/.claude/rules"
  {
    echo "---"
    echo "name: fake"
    [[ -n "$eff" ]] && echo "$eff"
    echo "---"
    echo "# Fake skill body"
    echo "Do fake things."
  } > "$sk/SKILL.md"
  echo "# loa" > "$d/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  echo "rule" > "$d/.claude/rules/r.md"
  ( cd "$d" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m tree )
}

@test "EA-1 task without .agent.skill exits 3 and writes nothing" {

2:# =============================================================================
3:# execute-agent.sh — agent-execution step for Loa Eval Sandbox trials
5:# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6). Fills the slot at the top of the
6:# grading step in run-eval.sh: a task that declares `.agent.skill` runs the
7:# headless Claude CLI inside the sandbox before its graders; every other task
8:# takes the pre-existing path untouched.
10:# What it does, in order:
11:#   1. Gate: no `.agent.skill` in the task YAML → exit 3, nothing written.
12:#   2. Materialize the prompt surface from $EVAL_PROMPT_TREE into the sandbox:
13:#        <ws>/.claude/skills/<skill>/        (SKILL.md + resources/)
14:#        <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      (+ .claude/rules/)
15:#        <ws>/CLAUDE.md                      → "@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
16:#        <ws>/.eval/skill-prompt.md          (SKILL.md body, frontmatter stripped)
17:#      The prompt tree is the ONLY thing that differs between A/B arms, so it
18:#      is recorded: prompt_tree_sha = `git rev-parse HEAD:.claude` of the tree,
19:#      prompt_tree_commit, and whether .claude/ had uncommitted changes.
20:#   3. Run:  claude -p "<task.prompt>" --output-format stream-json --verbose
21:#              --model $EVAL_MODEL [--effort <e>] --restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Write
22:#              --permission-mode acceptEdits --append-system-prompt-file <skill-prompt>
23:#              --max-turns $EVAL_MAX_TURNS
24:#      --restricted --tools names the SDD's fixed tool set EXACTLY: it removes the
25:#      code-running tools, ignores the operator's user/project/local settings (their
26:#      Bash(...) allow rules leaked into the sprint-237 A/B arms under --allowed-tools,
27:#      which only adds rules) and confines Read/Grep/Glob/Write to the sandbox.
28:#      Edit/MultiEdit are therefore unavailable; the transcript extractor below still
29:#      records them defensively.
30:#      cwd = sandbox; env-isolated (LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH / LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH and
31:#      TMPDIR into the sandbox; GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS_* unset;
32:#      HOME and PATH stay so the CLI finds its own credentials and toolchain).
33:#   4. Record <ws>/.eval/events.jsonl (raw stream), agent-output.json (the
34:#      `result` event) and executor.json:
35:#        {schema_version, skill, model_requested, model_id (the id the CLI
36:#         echoed — the modelUsage entry with the most output tokens), effort,
37:#         prompt_tree_sha, prompt_tree_commit, prompt_tree_dirty, exit_code,
38:#         is_error, duration_ms, num_turns, total_cost_usd, usage{…},
39:#         tool_writes:[{seq,tool,path}] in transcript order}
41:# Exit codes:
42:#   0  agent ran (its own verdict is the graders' business)
43:#   1  the CLI exited non-zero or timed out (executor.json still written)
44:#   2  infrastructure error (CLI binary missing, prompt tree lacks the skill)
45:#   3  task declares no agent (caller should not have called us)
47:# Env:
48:#   EVAL_MODEL          model passed to --model            (default claude-sonnet-5)
49:#   EVAL_EFFORT         override effort                    (default: task/skill)
50:#   EVAL_PROMPT_TREE    repo whose .claude/ is materialized (default: this repo)
51:#   EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN     CLI executable                     (default: claude)
52:#   EVAL_MAX_TURNS      --max-turns                        (default 40)
54:# Control arms (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.1):
55:#   LOA_EVAL_ARM          arm id (default baseline). Setting it at all is "arm
56:#                         mode": the prompt tree's .loa.config.yaml is also
57:#                         materialised so every arm sees the same config.
58:#   LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES  JSON object {toggle: false, …}; when unset the arm is
59:#                         resolved from LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE, else from
60:#                         evals/suites/<task dir name>.yaml (`ab.arms[]`)
61:#   LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT  recorded as source_commit (default: the prompt
62:#                         tree's HEAD)
63:#   Toggles are applied to the SANDBOX COPY only, after every materialisation
64:#   step and immediately before the executor starts; each is verified absent
65:#   afterwards and a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never
66:#   silently runs as its baseline):
67:#     companion_voice: false         flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false
68:#                                    in <ws>/.loa.config.yaml (yq)
69:#     karpathy_block: false          '## Karpathy Principles' section out of
70:#                                    <ws>/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md; Karpathy rows
71:#                                    out of <ws>/.claude/data/constraints.json if present
72:#     rule_files: false              stash-safety.md, skill-invariants.md out of <ws>/.claude/rules/

# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.

## Scope

Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).

## Origin

- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.

## Related rules

- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# build-review-corpus.sh — build the 10-PR review-recall corpus from this
     4	# repository's own history (cycle-124 Sprint 3, PRD FR-9 / SDD §3.6)
     5	#
     6	# Every planted defect is a real shipped fix, inverted: for a `defect` row the
     7	# PR under review turns the FIXED code (base/) back into the BUGGY code
     8	# (head/ = the fix commit's parent), so each defect has a real failing test in
     9	# history and a reviewer must reason about the code, not read a changelog.
    10	# Comment-only lines the fix ADDED (the "why this was wrong" prose) are removed
    11	# from base/ before diffing, so the inverted diff removes code, never a
    12	# confession. `clean` rows are forward fix commits (base = parent, head = fix,
    13	# tests included): a PR with nothing planted, so false positives are measurable.
    14	#
    15	# Inputs (committed):
    16	#   review-prs/corpus.tsv   fixture  kind  commit  file  defect_id  severity  category  must_match
    17	#   review-prs/prs.tsv      fixture  title  description
    18	# Outputs (committed, frozen by SHA256SUMS):
    19	#   review-prs/pr-NN/{PR.md,head.diff,base/…,head/…,fixture.yaml,
    20	#                     REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md}
    21	#   review-prs/manifests/pr-NN.json   HIDDEN — never copied into a sandbox
    22	#   review-prs/SHA256SUMS             the freeze; compare.sh pins its hash
    23	#
    24	# `must_match` is a literal substring that must occur on exactly ONE line of
    25	# the head/ file: that line is the defect's anchor (the grader accepts ±3).
    26	#
    27	# cycle-129: corpus.tsv also carries `record` rows (pr-11 … pr-18, sprints
    28	# 247–254) and `#` gap comments; those fixtures are built by
    29	# evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh (labels in the hidden labels/ dir)
    30	# and skipped here. The freeze below still covers every file in the corpus.
    31	# A rebuild here regenerates pr-01 … pr-10 from scratch; their hand-added
    32	# anchors[] (pr-02 D06, pr-05 D13) are not in corpus.tsv and must be re-added.
    33	#
    34	# Usage:
    35	#   build-review-corpus.sh            # (re)build everything + SHA256SUMS
    36	#   build-review-corpus.sh --verify   # sha256sum -c against the committed freeze
    37	# Exit: 0 ok, 1 verify failed / spec error, 2 usage
    38	# =============================================================================
    39	set -euo pipefail
    40	export LC_ALL=C
    41	
    42	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    43	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
    44	CORPUS="$HERE/review-prs"
    45	SPEC="$CORPUS/corpus.tsv"
    46	PRS="$CORPUS/prs.tsv"
    47	
    48	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--verify" ]]; then
    49	  [[ -f "$CORPUS/SHA256SUMS" ]] || { echo "ERROR: $CORPUS/SHA256SUMS missing" >&2; exit 1; }
    50	  ( cd "$CORPUS" && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS ) && echo "corpus OK: $(wc -l < "$CORPUS/SHA256SUMS") files match SHA256SUMS"
    51	  exit $?
    52	fi
    53	[[ $# -eq 0 ]] || { echo "usage: $0 [--verify]" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	[[ -f "$SPEC" && -f "$PRS" ]] || { echo "ERROR: corpus.tsv / prs.tsv missing under $CORPUS" >&2; exit 1; }
    55	
    56	python3 - "$REPO_ROOT" "$CORPUS" "$SPEC" "$PRS" <<'PY'
    57	import csv, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys
    58	repo, corpus, spec, prs = sys.argv[1:5]
    59	
    60	def git(*args, text=True):
    61	    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=text).stdout
    62	
    63	def show(rev, path):
    64	    try:
    65	        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "show", f"{rev}:{path}"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    66	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
    67	        return None
    68	
    69	COMMENT = {
    70	    ".sh": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".bash": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".py": re.compile(r"^\s*#"),
    71	    ".yaml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"), ".yml": re.compile(r"^\s*#"),
    72	    ".ts": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"), ".js": re.compile(r"^\s*(//|/\*|\*)"),
    73	}
    74	
    75	def added_comment_lines(commit, path):
    76	    """Line numbers (1-based, in the fixed file) of comment-only lines the fix added."""
    77	    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1]
    78	    rx = COMMENT.get(ext)
    79	    if rx is None:
    80	        return set()
    81	    diff = git("diff", "-U0", f"{commit}^", commit, "--", path)
    82	    out, new_no = set(), None
    83	    for line in diff.splitlines():
    84	        m = re.match(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,\d+)? @@", line)
    85	        if m:
    86	            new_no = int(m.group(1)); continue
    87	        if new_no is None or line.startswith("+++") or line.startswith("---"):
    88	            continue
    89	        if line.startswith("+"):
    90	            if rx.match(line[1:]):
    91	                out.add(new_no)
    92	            new_no += 1
    93	        # '-' lines do not advance the new-file counter
    94	    return out
    95	
    96	# cycle-129: `#` lines are comments (record-fixture gaps) and `record` rows are
    97	# built by evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh, not here
    98	_spec_lines = [l for l in open(spec, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines() if l and not l.startswith("#")]
    99	rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(_spec_lines, delimiter="\t", quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE) if r["kind"] != "record"]
   100	prmeta = {r["fixture"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(prs, encoding="utf-8"), delimiter="\t", quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE)}
   101	fixtures = {}
   102	for r in rows:
   103	    fixtures.setdefault(r["fixture"], []).append(r)
   104	
   105	REVIEW_INSTR = """# Review instructions
   106	
   107	This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.
   108	
   109	- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
   110	- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
   111	- `base/` — every touched file before the change
   112	- `head/` — every touched file after the change
   113	
   114	Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.
   115	
   116	Write your review to `review.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your reviewer skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
   117	"""
   118	AUDIT_INSTR = REVIEW_INSTR.replace("# Review instructions", "# Audit instructions") \
   119	    .replace("Review the change as the senior technical reviewer", "Audit the change as the security auditor") \
   120	    .replace("Write your review to `review.md`", "Write your audit to `audit.md`") \
   121	    .replace("your reviewer skill's output format", "your auditor skill's output format")
   122	
   123	manifests_dir = os.path.join(corpus, "manifests")
   124	os.makedirs(manifests_dir, exist_ok=True)
   125	errors = []
   126	built = []
   127	for fx, frows in fixtures.items():
   128	    fdir = os.path.join(corpus, fx)
   129	    for sub in ("base", "head"):
   130	        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(fdir, sub), ignore_errors=True)
   131	    os.makedirs(fdir, exist_ok=True)
   132	    defects, files = [], []
   133	    seen_files = set()
   134	    for r in frows:
   135	        kind, commit, path = r["kind"], r["commit"], r["file"]
   136	        if path in seen_files:
   137	            errors.append(f"{fx}: {path} listed twice (two commits on one file cannot compose)"); continue
   138	        seen_files.add(path)
   139	        if kind == "defect":
   140	            fixed, buggy = show(commit, path), show(f"{commit}^", path)
   141	            if fixed is None or buggy is None:
   142	                errors.append(f"{fx}: {commit}:{path} or its parent is missing"); continue
   143	            drop = added_comment_lines(commit, path)
   144	            base_lines = [l for i, l in enumerate(fixed.splitlines(keepends=True), 1) if i not in drop]
   145	            base_text, head_text = "".join(base_lines), buggy
   146	        elif kind == "clean":
   147	            base_text, head_text = show(f"{commit}^", path), show(commit, path)
   148	            if head_text is None:
   149	                errors.append(f"{fx}: {commit}:{path} missing"); continue
   150	        else:
   151	            errors.append(f"{fx}: unknown kind {kind}"); continue
   152	        if base_text is not None:
   153	            bp = os.path.join(fdir, "base", path); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(bp), exist_ok=True)
   154	            open(bp, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(base_text)
   155	        hp = os.path.join(fdir, "head", path); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(hp), exist_ok=True)
   156	        open(hp, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(head_text)
   157	        files.append((path, base_text is not None))
   158	        if kind == "defect":
   159	            needle = r["must_match"]
   160	            hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(head_text.splitlines(), 1) if needle in l]
   161	            if len(hits) != 1:
   162	                errors.append(f"{fx}/{r['defect_id']}: must_match {needle!r} matched {len(hits)} lines in head/{path} (need exactly 1)"); continue
   163	            defects.append({
   164	                "id": r["defect_id"], "file": path, "anchor_line": hits[0], "must_match": needle,
   165	                "severity": r["severity"], "category": r["category"], "source_commit": commit, "synthetic": False,
   166	            })
   167	    # head.diff — one unified diff per file, a/<path> b/<path>
   168	    parts = []
   169	    for path, has_base in files:
   170	        bp = os.path.join(fdir, "base", path) if has_base else "/dev/null"
   171	        hp = os.path.join(fdir, "head", path)
   172	        p = subprocess.run(["diff", "-u", "--label", f"a/{path}", "--label", f"b/{path}", bp, hp], capture_output=True, text=True)
   173	        if p.returncode not in (0, 1):
   174	            errors.append(f"{fx}: diff failed for {path}: {p.stderr.strip()}"); continue
   175	        if p.stdout:
   176	            parts.append(f"diff --git a/{path} b/{path}\n" + p.stdout)
   177	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "head.diff"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(parts))
   178	    meta = prmeta.get(fx, {"title": fx, "description": ""})
   179	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "PR.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(f"# {meta['title']}\n\n{meta['description']}\n")
   180	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(REVIEW_INSTR)
   181	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(AUDIT_INSTR)
   182	    open(os.path.join(fdir, "fixture.yaml"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(
   183	        f'name: {fx}\nversion: "1.0.0"\nlanguage: mixed\nruntime: none\ndependency_strategy: none\n'
   184	        f'description: "review-recall corpus PR {fx} (cycle-124 FR-9); planted defects live in the hidden manifest"\n'
   185	        f'difficulty: intermediate\ndomain: framework\ndeprecated: false\n')
   186	    json.dump({"fixture": fx, "defects": defects}, open(os.path.join(manifests_dir, f"{fx}.json"), "w"), indent=2)
   187	    built.append((fx, len(files), len(defects)))
   188	
   189	if errors:
   190	    print("\n".join("ERROR: " + e for e in errors), file=sys.stderr)
   191	    sys.exit(1)
   192	
   193	# freeze
   194	entries = []
   195	for root, _dirs, fnames in os.walk(corpus):
   196	    for f in fnames:
   197	        rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), corpus)
   198	        if rel in ("SHA256SUMS",):
   199	            continue
   200	        entries.append(rel)
   201	import hashlib
   202	lines = []
   203	for rel in sorted(entries):
   204	    h = hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(corpus, rel), "rb").read()).hexdigest()
   205	    lines.append(f"{h}  {rel}")
   206	open(os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS"), "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
   207	total = sum(d for _, _, d in built)
   208	for fx, nf, nd in built:
   209	    print(f"{fx}: {nf} file(s), {nd} planted defect(s)")
   210	print(f"built {len(built)} fixtures, {total} planted defects, {len(lines)} files frozen in SHA256SUMS")
   211	PY

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.5 (FR-2, SDD D-2.2)
     4	#
     5	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh over a tiny record tree built from
     6	# evals/tests/fixtures/seed-record/: a throwaway repo with base, head and fix
     7	# commits and a record branch carrying one round-1 review file. Proves: a
     8	# finding whose fix touches its file is kept; a finding whose file the fix
     9	# never touches is dropped by the rule; fix rows come from the fix hunks; a
    10	# finding carrying a secret is rejected; the approved-by header is required;
    11	# the labels stay out of the sandbox-copied fixture dir; SHA256SUMS covers it.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	setup() {
    15	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    16	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    17	  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh"
    18	  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
    19	  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/seed-record"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sc.XXXXXX")"
    21	  G="$T/repo"; C="$T/corpus"; K="$T/tasks"
    22	  mkdir -p "$G" "$C/pr-01" "$C/labels" "$K"
    23	  # the fake key is assembled here so no literal key shape is ever committed
    24	  FAKE_KEY="AKIA$(printf 'QZ%.0s' 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8)"
    25	  gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t "$@"; }
    26	  git -C "$G" init -q -b main
    27	  cp -R "$FX/base/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "base"
    28	  cp -R "$FX/head/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "feat: sprint-901 the input helper (round 1)"
    29	  cp -R "$FX/fix/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix: sprint-901 review round 1"
    30	  BASE="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~2)"; HEAD_C="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~1)"; FIX="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)"
    31	  gc checkout -q --orphan record/cycle-901-a2a
    32	  git -C "$G" rm -rq --cached . ; find "$G" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
    33	  mkdir -p "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901"
    34	  sed "s/@SECRET@/$FAKE_KEY/" "$FX/engineer-feedback-r1.md.in" > "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md"
    35	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "record"; gc checkout -q main
    36	  # a minimal corpus: the instruction templates and the corpus spec header
    37	  echo "# Review instructions" > "$C/pr-01/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    38	  echo "# Audit instructions" > "$C/pr-01/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    39	  printf 'fixture\tkind\tcommit\tfile\tdefect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tmust_match\n' > "$C/corpus.tsv"
    40	  ARGS=(--repo "$G" --corpus "$C" --tasks-dir "$K" --base "$BASE" --head "$HEAD_C" --fix "$FIX" --feedback engineer-feedback-r1.md --out "$C/pr-90")
    41	}
    42	
    43	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    44	
    45	@test "SC-1 seeding builds the fixture; labels stay hidden; the fix-touches-file rule keeps a.sh and drops b.sh; fix rows come from the fix hunks" {
    46	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    47	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    48	  for f in fixture.yaml head.diff PR.md REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md head/scripts/a.sh head/scripts/b.sh base/scripts/a.sh; do
    49	    [ -f "$C/pr-90/$f" ]
    50	  done
    51	  grep -q '^sprint: 901$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    52	  grep -q "^head_commit: \"$HEAD_C\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    53	  grep -q "^fix_commit: \"$FIX\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    54	  grep -q '^record_ref: "record/cycle-901-a2a"$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    55	  grep -q 'grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    56	  # the labels never sit in the directory the sandbox copies
    57	  [ -z "$(find "$C/pr-90" -name 'labels*' -o -name '*.dropped.txt')" ]
    58	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
    59	  [ "$(head -1 "$L")" = "# approved-by: pending" ]
    60	  grep -qx "$(printf 'defect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tfile\tmust_match\tlabel_source\tsource')" "$L"
    61	  # kept: the a.sh finding (its fix touches a.sh), anchored where the fix inserts
    62	  # the missing check (after `local v="$1"`) and on the short function's definition
    63	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4 "|" $6}' "$L" | sort -u)" = "scripts/a.sh|review" ]
    64	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'local v="$1"'
    65	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'check_input() {'
    66	  # dropped by the rule: b.sh (the fix never touches it); the prose finding; the previous-round section is never read
    67	  grep -q 'fix commit does not touch scripts/b.sh' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    68	  grep -q 'no code locus' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    69	  ! grep -q 'must never be read' "$L" "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    70	  # fix rows: one per fix hunk, on a.sh and c.sh, sourced fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>
    71	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $4}' "$L" | sort | tr '\n' ,)" = "scripts/a.sh,scripts/c.sh," ]
    72	  awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $7}' "$L" | grep -qE "^fix/${FIX:0:12}:[0-9]+-[0-9]+$"
    73	  # the hidden manifest, the tasks, the corpus row and the freeze
    74	  M="$C/manifests/pr-90.json"
    75	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved' "$M")" = "false" ]
    76	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects | length' "$M")" = "1" ]
    77	  [ "$(jq -r '.fix_regions | length' "$M")" = "2" ]
    78	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects[0].label_source' "$M")" = "review" ]
    79	  [ -f "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml" ] && [ -f "$K/audit-recall/audit-pr-90.yaml" ]
    80	  [ "$(yq -r '.graders[0].args[0]' "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml")" = "pr-90" ]
    81	  grep -q "^pr-90	record	${HEAD_C:0:8}	labels/pr-90.tsv" "$C/corpus.tsv"
    82	  run "$SEED" --check --corpus "$C"
    83	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    84	}
    85	
    86	@test "SC-2 a finding carrying a secret is rejected without its text; nothing written carries the key and every file passes no-secrets.sh" {
    87	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    88	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    89	  grep -q 'secret pattern in the finding text' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    90	  ! grep -rqF "$FAKE_KEY" "$C"
    91	  ! awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4}' "$C/labels/pr-90.tsv" | grep -q 'c.sh'
    92	  run bash "$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/no-secrets.sh" "$C"
    93	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    94	}
    95	
    96	@test "SC-3 recall-vs-defects.sh grades the seeded label: the anchor detects it, a fix region is not refuted, an unrelated line is" {
    97	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    98	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    99	  local at; at="$(jq -r '.defects[0].anchor_line' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")"
   100	  W="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$W"
   101	  printf '%s\n' "- HIGH head/scripts/a.sh:$at accepts an empty value" "- LOW head/scripts/c.sh:3 prints the token" \
   102	    "- LOW head/scripts/b.sh:2 loops forever" > "$W/review.md"
   103	  EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$C/manifests" run "$GRADER" "$W" pr-90 review.md
   104	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   105	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.recall == 1')" = "true" ]
   106	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_cited')" = "3" ]
   107	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_refuted')" = "1" ]
   108	}
   109	
   110	@test "SC-4 the approved-by header is required; --approve records the approver, marks the manifest approved and refreezes" {
   111	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
   112	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   113	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
   114	  cp "$L" "$T/keep.tsv"
   115	  tail -n +2 "$T/keep.tsv" > "$L"
   116	  run "$SEED" --build-manifest pr-90 --corpus "$C"
   117	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   118	  grep -q 'approved-by' <<<"$output"
   119	  cp "$T/keep.tsv" "$L"

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2
# (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol; SDD §3.6 "compare.sh refuses drift")
#
# compare.sh freshness rule: a baseline that carries prompt_tree_sha is
# refused (exit 2) when it equals the prompt tree under comparison
# (tautological), when its captured_at_commit predates the suite's
# ab.floor_commit (stale), or when the corpus manifest hash drifted.
# --ab mode compares two arm run dirs on recall / false positives / tokens
# and refuses invalid runs (model skew, dirty trees, identical prompt trees).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  COMPARE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/compare.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bf.XXXXXX")"
  # A prompt tree with two commits: floor (c1) and a later one (c2).
  TREE="$T/tree"; mkdir -p "$TREE/.claude"
  ( cd "$TREE" && git init -q \
    && echo a > "$TREE/.claude/a" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c1 \
    && echo b > "$TREE/.claude/b" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c2 )
  C1="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD~1)"; C2="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
  TREE_SHA="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD:.claude)"
  OLD_TREE_SHA="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD~1:.claude)"
  # corpus manifest + suite with ab block
  mkdir -p "$T/corpus" "$T/suites"
  echo "abc  pr-01/head.diff" > "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
  CORPUS_SHA="$(sha256sum "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  cat > "$T/suites/rr.yaml" <<YAML
name: rr
ab:
  floor_commit: "$C1"
  corpus_manifest: "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
YAML
  cat > "$T/results.jsonl" <<'JSONL'
{"run_id":"r","task_id":"review-pr-01","trial":1,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","duration_ms":1,"model_version":"m1","status":"completed","graders":[],"composite":{"strategy":"all_must_pass","pass":true,"score":100},"error":null,"schema_version":1}
JSONL
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

baseline() {  # baseline <prompt_tree_sha> <captured_at_commit> <corpus_sha256>
  cat > "$T/rr.baseline.yaml" <<YAML
version: 1
suite: rr
model_version: "m1"
recorded_at: "2026-01-01"
prompt_tree_sha: "$1"
captured_at_commit: "$2"
corpus_sha256: "$3"
tasks:
  review-pr-01:
    pass_rate: 1.0
    trials: 1
    mean_score: 100
    status: active
YAML
}

@test "BF-1 a baseline whose prompt_tree_sha equals the current prompt tree is refused as tautological" {
  baseline "$TREE_SHA" "$C2" "$CORPUS_SHA"
  run "$COMPARE" --results "$T/results.jsonl" --baseline "$T/rr.baseline.yaml" --suite-file "$T/suites/rr.yaml" --prompt-tree "$TREE"
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
  grep -qi 'tautological' <<<"$output"
}

@test "BF-2 a baseline captured on a commit that is not a descendant of the suite floor is refused as stale" {
  local root; root="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)"
  baseline "$OLD_TREE_SHA" "$root" "$CORPUS_SHA"
  cat > "$T/suites/rr.yaml" <<YAML
name: rr
ab:
  floor_commit: "$C2"
  corpus_manifest: "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
YAML
  run "$COMPARE" --results "$T/results.jsonl" --baseline "$T/rr.baseline.yaml" --suite-file "$T/suites/rr.yaml" --prompt-tree "$TREE"
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
  grep -qi 'predates' <<<"$output"

# cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1). Each arm is applied by
  # execute-agent.sh (LOA_EVAL_ARM=<id>) to the SANDBOX COPY of the prompt
  # surface only, after materialisation and immediately before the executor
  # starts; the source tree is never edited. run-arms.sh drives the arms
  # against a detached worktree pinned at --source-commit.
  #   id           canonical arm id (results rows and reports key on it)
  #   description  what the arm removes, and what it does not
  #   toggles      toggle -> false; an unknown toggle fails the trial (exit 2)
  #   informational  true: the arm reports a yield figure only; its verdict
  #                can never license removing the control
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_companion
      description: >-
        flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice set false in the sandbox
        .loa.config.yaml. The companion voice is a floor key that no profile
        can remove; this arm measures its yield only.
      informational: true
      toggles:
        companion_voice: false
    - id: no_karpathy
      description: >-
        the '## Karpathy Principles' section removed from the sandbox
        CLAUDE.loa.md (and any Karpathy row from a sandbox constraints.json).
        It removes the kernel block only, not the SURGICAL review axis in
        reviewing-code/SKILL.md or the surgical-diff hook.
      toggles:
        karpathy_block: false
    - id: no_rule_files
      description: "stash-safety.md and skill-invariants.md removed from the sandbox .claude/rules/"
      toggles:
        rule_files: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule (PRD FR-2; report.sh --arms applies it).
  # An arm reads `no recall loss` only when every condition holds; a violated
  # condition reads `recall loss`; anything missing reads `inconclusive`.
  threshold:
    # every (fixture, arm) cell needs this many completed trials
    trials_required: 3
    # full = every fixture in the batch for every arm; a missing cell is inconclusive
    coverage_required: full
    # the upper bound of the bootstrap interval on (baseline - arm) mean
    # recall must not exceed this (= ci.regression_threshold)
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    # the arm's worst trial-mean recall may sit at most this far below the baseline's worst
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    # refuted share (cited findings matching no feedback label and no fix
    # region, over cited findings) may rise at most this much over the baseline
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
  # cycle-129 FR-2 control arms (SDD D-2.1); see review-recall.yaml for the
  # key reference. Toggles apply to the sandbox copy only.
  arms:
    - id: baseline
      description: "the pinned source tree's prompt surface, unchanged"
      toggles: {}
    - id: no_audit_delta
      description: >-
        the audit's review-delta paragraph removed from the sandbox
        auditing-security/SKILL.md: the paragraph containing "look for what
        the review did not" when present, else the "Confirm the review's
        demotions independently" paragraph (the delta instruction as written
        at 864069f2). A missing paragraph fails the trial (exit 2).
      toggles:
        audit_delta_instruction: false

  # Pre-registered verdict rule; same keys and meaning as review-recall.yaml.
  threshold:
    trials_required: 3
    coverage_required: full
    mean_recall_max_drop: 0.10
    min_trial_recall_max_drop: 0.15
    refuted_share_max_rise: 0.10
    bootstrap:
      method: percentile
      level: 0.90

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--results-root", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--suites-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--suites", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--partial", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--date", default=datetime.date.today().isoformat())
    args = ap.parse_args()

    suites = [s for s in args.suites.split(",") if s] or sorted(
        s for s in ("review-recall", "audit-recall") if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(args.results_root, s)))
    if not suites:
        print(f"arms-report: no suite results under {args.results_root}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    for s in suites:
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(args.results_root, s)):
            print(f"arms-report: no results for suite {s} under {args.results_root}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        st = {}
        sp = os.path.join(args.results_root, s, "STATUS.json")
        if os.path.isfile(sp):
            st = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
        if st.get("state") != "complete" and not args.partial:
            print(f"arms-report: {s} STATUS.json state is {st.get('state', 'missing')!r}, not 'complete'; "
                  "refusing to write a verdict report (pass --partial for an inconclusive interim report)",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

    lines = [f"# Control-arm report — {args.date}", ""]
    if args.partial:
        lines += ["> **PARTIAL REPORT.** Written with `--partial` before every run completed: every verdict "
                  "below reads `inconclusive` and none licenses a deletion (SDD D-2.3).", ""]
    lines += ["Generated by `evals/harness/report.sh --arms` from `" + args.results_root + "`. "
              "Recall is graded by `recall-vs-defects.sh` (planted defects and approved record labels); "
              "refuted share counts cited findings that match neither a label nor a fix region. "
              "A deletion that relies on an arm requires the lead to read that arm's missed labels and record the reading.", ""]
    for s in suites:
        suite_report(args.results_root, args.suites_dir, s, args.partial, lines)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(args.out)), exist_ok=True)
    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n")
    print(args.out)
    return 0

show_help() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME --type prd|sdd|sprint|bug-triage|translation|decisions|map|spike|glossary --file <path>
       [--base-file <path>] [--ledger <path>] [--json]

Validate a Loa planning artifact against its skill-defined structural
contract (grep-based, fail-closed).

Options:
  --type TYPE   Artifact type: prd | sdd | sprint | bug-triage | translation | decisions | map | spike | glossary (required)
  --file PATH   Artifact file to validate (required). For --type translation,
                may also be a directory (validates every *.md under it).
  --base-file PATH
                decisions: the pre-write ledger the append-only check compares
                against (default: the copy at git merge-base origin/main HEAD)
  --ledger PATH prd: the decision ledger the [ASSUMPTION decision] tags cite
                (default: grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml)
  --json        Emit a JSON result object to stdout
  -h, --help    Show this help message

sprint: plans dated from 2026-10-14 end every task line with
  ' · kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' (older plans WARN).

Exit codes:
  0  pass (WARN-level info may still be printed)
  1  fail (exact repair text on stderr)
  2  usage error (missing arguments, unknown type, file not found)
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --type) TYPE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --file) FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --base-file) BASE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --ledger) LEDGER_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS=(
    "Security Considerations"
)

validate_sprint() {
    local sprint_headings
    sprint_headings=$(grep -nE '^## Sprint [0-9]' -- "$FILE" || true)

    if [[ -z "$sprint_headings" ]]; then
        violations+=("no '## Sprint N' blocks found — sprint.md must contain at least one sprint block")
        return
    fi

    local last_sprint_heading="" last_sprint_lineno=0
    while IFS=: read -r lineno heading; do
        [[ -z "$lineno" ]] && continue
        last_sprint_heading="$heading"
        last_sprint_lineno="$lineno"
        local block
        block=$(awk -v start="$lineno" '
            NR > start && /^## Sprint [0-9]/ { exit }
            NR > start { print }
        ' < "$FILE")
        local sec
        for sec in "${SPRINT_REQUIRED_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                violations+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) is missing required section '### $sec' — see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md")
            fi
        done
        for sec in "${SPRINT_WARN_SECTIONS[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qE "^### ($sec)\$" <<< "$block"; then
                warnings+=("sprint block '${heading# }' (line $lineno) has no '### $sec' section — recommended for security-relevant sprints")
            fi
        done
    done <<< "$sprint_headings"

    # @guard validator:sprint.goal-ids
    # Goal ID coverage: every G-N referenced in the plan body must appear in
    # a goal-mapping table under any '## Appendix' section.
    local appendix_body
    appendix_body=$(awk '
        /^## Appendix/ { found=1; next }
        found && /^## / { found=0 }
        found { print }
    ' < "$FILE")

    local body_goal_ids
    body_goal_ids=$(grep -oE 'G-[0-9]+' -- "$FILE" | sort -u || true)
    if [[ -n "$body_goal_ids" ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r gid; do
            [[ -z "$gid" ]] && continue
            if ! grep -qwF "$gid" <<< "$appendix_body"; then
                violations+=("goal ID $gid appears in the plan but not in any '## Appendix' goal table — add a row for $gid")
            fi
        done <<< "$body_goal_ids"
    fi

    validate_sprint_deferred
    validate_sprint_seams
    validate_sprint_kinds
    validate_sprint_beads

    # Final sprint E2E/validation task (WARN only).
    local last_block
    last_block=$(awk -v start="$last_sprint_lineno" 'NR > start { print }' < "$FILE")
    if ! grep -qiE 'E2E|end-to-end' <<< "$last_block"; then
        warnings+=("final sprint block '${last_sprint_heading# }' has no E2E/end-to-end validation task")
    fi
}
